sections.html:
The seat of Cache County, Logan lies about 47 miles north of Ogden where Cache Valley meets the Bear River Mountains. It grew from 48,174 residents in 2010 to 52,778 in 2020, with an estimate of 55,576 for July 2025. Median age was 24.2 in 2020, and with Utah State University anchoring the city, rentals near campus make up a large slice of the market.

East of downtown the streets climb across terraces called benches, old Lake Bonneville sediment, and west of town the ground levels out into farmland and marsh. Location on that terrain changes what an inspector examines. Lots on the benches raise slope and runoff questions, and lots in the flat west sit closer to farmland and marsh.

Summers are warm and mostly dry. Winters are cold, with about 18.97 inches of precipitation and 61.5 inches of snow in a typical year, and the record low is minus 25 degrees. Snow sits on roofs for months, and a vacant house risks frozen pipes.

If you cannot heat or check on an empty house through the cold months, closing before winter can save you a costly repair.

Utah State University and its Space Dynamics Laboratory are the largest employers in Logan. Others include ICON Health and Fitness, Campbell Scientific, Logan Regional Hospital, JBS USA, Schreiber Foods and the local school districts. Education, manufacturing, medical services, agriculture and retail make up the economy.

If you own a rental close to campus, let the academic calendar guide your closing date, because tenant turnover follows it.

Eight public schools belong to Logan City School District: six elementary schools, a middle school and Logan High School. Parts of Logan fall under the Cache County School District instead, so check the boundary for any particular address. Bridgerland Technical College offers certificate programs.

Connect Transit is a zero-fare bus system with 15 routes serving Logan, North Logan and River Heights, and Logan-Cache Airport handles general aviation. City business licensing is at Logan City Hall, 290 N 100 W, phone 435-716-9230.

A landlord business license is mandatory in Logan for each owner of a rental unit, and any LLC, trust or corporation that owns one needs its own license. Exempt are owner-occupied homes rented only during a hospital or nursing home stay or a temporary absence of three years or less.

Occupancy ruleLimit
General zonesThree unrelated people, or one family plus one additional person
Campus Residential zonesUp to six unrelated people, no more than two per bedroom
Notice to tenantsIn the lease or on a zoning occupancy disclosure form
Request from a code official or police officerLease or form provided within seven days

Rentals must also follow the city's Fit Premise Ordinance in Municipal Code Chapter 15.25. A unit that was never legally created may have to apply for grandfathered status. Before you sell a rental by campus, bring the license and occupancy paperwork up to date, since an investor will want to see it. Changes to ownership or agent contact information need an amendment form through the business licensing office.

The year starts with July valuation notices. Appeals run August to September, tax notices come in October, and payment is due November 30. Anything unpaid for the current year turns delinquent in December.

Prior-year delinquencies are posted in January, and by month's end the Treasurer either collects or notifies new owners. A seller who owes taxes should expect the title company to settle them out of the proceeds.

The state exempts 45 percent of a primary home's market value, as long as the owner lives there for 183 consecutive days. After a purchase, the buyer files Form TC-473A by September 15, and late filings are refused.

Deeds are recorded by the Cache County Recorder. Recording fees change from time to time, so ask what the current charge is before closing.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Logan house work?
sections.html:
Think of a cash sale as an ordinary closing with the bank removed. The buyer looks over the property and presents an offer, then a title company deals with liens, taxes and the deed.

  1. Tell us about the house, its tenants and the lease end dates.
  2. Weigh the offer and proposed closing date.
  3. Sign at the title company, which sends the deed to Cache County for recording.

This route draws landlords with a lease running to a set date, heirs managing a house from afar, and owners unwilling to pay for repairs. When tenants stay in place, the buyer can ask to see the lease and the occupancy disclosure form.

A title company sits in the middle of every Logan sale, cash or financed. Its staff trace ownership, flag liens and unpaid taxes, draw up the settlement statement and get the deed recorded. Payoffs and any tax balance appear as separate lines and come off the top of your proceeds.

Request the settlement statement a day before signing and compare it with your own numbers. Should a rental license, a lease or an old lien raise a question, the title officer can usually name the paper that settles it.

sections.h2: Is a direct sale right for you?
sections.html: A traditional listing suits a house in good shape when you can wait through showings, an inspection and a buyer's loan approval. A direct sale suits a house that needs work, a rental with a lease or an owner who is far away. You skip repairs, staging and open houses, and you pick a closing date that fits your move. Compare what a listing would leave you after repairs, commission and carrying costs with a written offer, and ask for proof of funds before you agree to anything. Before you decide, think about how long the house has been empty or rented, what repairs a buyer's inspector would flag, and whether your tax and utility bills are current. Writing those answers down gives you a clear picture of what a listing would really require.

sections.h2: Timing a sale around tenants and the calendar
sections.html: With a tenant in the house, the lease decides what is possible. Share the end date and the notice terms with any buyer at the start, and expect a cash buyer to ask whether the tenant plans to stay. If the house is empty, heating it through winter costs money, so a closing before the cold sets in avoids both bills and frozen-pipe risk. Gather the deed, the latest tax notice, any landlord license paperwork and the lease before you call, and ask the title company to confirm which taxes are owed. If tenants are staying, a short note to them about showings or a buyer's visit keeps things friendly and the house easier to sell.

faqs.q: How many people live in Logan, Utah?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 52,778, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 55,576.

faqs.q: Do I need a landlord license to rent a house in Logan?
faqs.a: Yes. Logan requires a landlord business license for every owner of a rental unit, with a narrow exception for a temporary absence of three years or less. Call 435-716-9230 for fees and renewal.

faqs.q: When are Cache County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By November 30. The Treasurer mails tax notices in October, and unpaid current-year taxes become delinquent in December.

faqs.q: How many unrelated people can live in a Logan house?
faqs.a: Generally three unrelated people, or one family plus one more person. Campus Residential zones allow up to six, with no more than two per bedroom.

faqs.q: What is the largest employer in Logan?
faqs.a: Utah State University and its Space Dynamics Laboratory are the largest employers in Logan.
